svg.title: Meshing and rendering
svg.desc: Exploded mesh slabs make draw order tangible before the shared geometry branches to data or pixels.

text.tspan: Transparency order is part of the data path.

g.title: Opaque geometry writes depth first
g.desc: Solid faces draw first and establish the depth buffer for cheaper rejection behind them.

g.title: Cutout geometry discards empty texels
g.desc: Leaves and panes keep hard alpha edges without blending while still using depth testing.

g.title: Transparent geometry blends last
g.desc: Water and stained glass are sorted back to front after the depth-writing layers.

g.title: Portable output keeps the mesh as data
g.desc: GLB, glTF, USDZ, and NUCM feed viewers, DCC tools, and caches.

g.title: The native renderer turns the same mesh into pixels
g.desc: Camera, grid, materials, and lighting produce stills or deterministic animation frames.

text.tspan: Mesh once, then keep the geometry or draw it
The mesher builds three ordered layers over one atlas; export and native rendering share that result.
